text.p: MELBOURNE, Sept 10 - National Australia Bank (NAB) Ltd on Tuesday recommended the consolidation of all financial system supervisors under a mega-supervisor as part of its submission to the government's Wallis inquiry into financial regulation.
"This (mega-supervisor) would cover areas such as banking, payments, insurance, superannuation, financial markets and consumer issues," NAB said in a statement.

It said such a mega-supervisor would comprise of three units, including the Reserve Bank of Australia as the operator of monetary policy, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission and a separate board for prudential supervision.
NAB said the governor of the Reserve Bank should chair the board governing prudential supervision.
NAB also recommended that financial institutions other than banks be allowed to operate in the payments system, provided specified capital and liquidity requirements were met.
It said the six pillars policy operated by the former Labor government, which prevented mergers between the big four banks and the two big superannuation funds, was now outdated.

NAB, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, Westpac Banking Corp Ltd, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, the Australian Mutual Provident Society and National Mutual Holdings Ltd are seen as the six pillars.

"For the purposes of competition, the 'markets' should be more broadly defined. That definition should recognise that the market for banking and financial services is at least national and covers all areas of financial activity," NAB said.
NAB also said the inquiry recommendations should provide for the emergence of new structures in the financial services system such as holding companies that include banks.
